title: wt remove <work> --dry-run --json
description: What `wt remove <work>` would do, and the token that holds a later removal to it. Printed by `wt remove <work> --dry-run --json`, and by `wt remove <work> --json` without --yes, as the only thing on stdout; nothing is changed. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

repo.description: The main checkout; null outside a repository.

token.description: Names this plan; pass it to wt remove --yes --json --expect. Null when the removal would refuse, or on error.

error.description: Why the removal would refuse, or why no plan could be made.

path.description: The checkout, absolute; null when no worktree was found.

adminDir.description: The worktree's own git dir, .git/worktrees/<id>; null when it cannot be read.

detached.description: No branch is checked out: no branch is touched.

bases.description: What merged is measured against, first first: origin/<trunk> as last fetched, then <trunk>. Remove never fetches.

dirty.description: Anything uncommitted, submodules included, whatever git's config says.

statusError.description: Why the status could not be read; the removal refuses.

hiddenFiles.description: Unedited files git status is told not to look at (assume-unchanged, skip-worktree).

movedSubmodules.description: Submodules checked out at another commit than the recorded one.

nestedWorktrees.description: Other worktrees whose checkouts are inside this one.

operation.description: A git operation stopped halfway there; sequencer is a cherry-pick or revert sequence whose HEAD marker is gone.

sessions.description: The Claude sessions working in the checkout, other than the one running wt.

sessionsError.description: Why the sessions could not be listed; the removal refuses without --force.

unreachable.description: Each tip whose commits nothing surviving the removal would hold.

reachError.description: Why that could not be worked out; the removal refuses.

keepSuperset.description: Since 1.1.0. --keep-superset was given: the worktree's Superset workspace is left, and Superset is not asked anything. The token covers it.

force.description: Bare --force was given: the problems with force true do not refuse. False for --force=<list>, whose categories forceWith names.

forceWith.description: Since 1.2.0. The --force categories given, all five for bare --force; empty without it. The token covers them.

problems.description: Every problem with the removal; those that refuse it are all of them, less the ones whose forceWith is in the top-level forceWith.

code.description: dirty: anything uncommitted, submodules included, or a submodule not at its recorded commit. statusUnknown: git status, the git dir or HEAD could not be read. session: a Claude session is in it, idle or busy. sessionsUnknown: claude agents failed. lockHeld: git's worktree lock, and its holder is still running. operation: a rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress. hiddenChanges: files git status is told not to look at. headUnreachable: HEAD holds commits no surviving ref or worktree would. reachUnknown: what would be lost could not be worked out. submoduleUnreachable: a submodule commit only this worktree's copy holds. nestedWorktree: another worktree is inside it. quarantineUnusable: the --quarantine folder exists, is on another volume, or is inside the repository. planChanged (result only): --expect named another plan. The codes shared with sweep-plan's kept mean the same there.

force.description: --force goes past it: somebody's claim on the checkout, not work that would be lost.

forceWith.description: Since 1.2.0. The --force category that goes past it; null when force is false. A session problem is either idle-sessions or busy-sessions: idle and busy sessions are two problems.

forceCategory.description: What --force=<list> names; bare --force is all of them. idle-sessions: an idle Claude session in it. busy-sessions: a busy one, and idle ones too. sessions-unknown: claude agents failed. hidden-files: files git status is told not to look at, unedited. lock: git's lock, its holder still running.

tip.description: Null when the branch is already gone.

merge.description: merged: base contains the tip. applied: every commit is on base under another id, byte for byte. unmerged: base lacks commits of it. unknown: no trunk to compare with, or the branch is gone.

base.description: The base the standing is about.

ahead.description: Commits base lacks; meaningful for unmerged and applied.

pullRequest.description: A pull request GitHub merged into trunk at exactly tip, as wt list or wt sweep recorded it; it makes an unmerged branch deletable.

outcome.description: delete: merged, applied or pullRequest; deleted after the checkout, only at tip. keep: an unmerged branch wt made; renamed to keepAs. none: left as it is; reason says why. The same names recovery.json's branch.plan uses.

holder.description: Whoever wt worked out is behind it.

held.description: Its holder is still there. A held lock refuses without --force; a stale one is released.

kind.description: branch: the branch the removal deletes; listed, not refused. head: the checkout's HEAD; refuses. submodule: a submodule's commits; refuses.

path.description: For submodule: the submodule, relative to the checkout.

restoreCommand.description: For branch: the argv that brings the commits back once the branch is gone.
